New machine. Its objects are: gefona, suvuben, motufos, tafuna, neterus, nigogik.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing three of the six objects together. Whichever way the machine works, a lit or unlit result splits the 30 possible explanations (15 pairs × 2 rules) evenly, 15 and 15.

TEST: gefona, suvuben, motufos
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

Of the 30 possible explanations, 15 fit the first result. Under the "one nexiom" rule, 12 pairs have at least one nexiom among gefona, suvuben and motufos. Under the "both nexioms" rule, 3 pairs have both nexioms in that group.

Testing gefona with tafuna splits these 15 nearly in half:
- **Lights up (7 cases):** only possible under the "one nexiom" rule, with gefona or tafuna as a nexiom.
- **Stays dark (8 cases):** either the "one nexiom" rule with neither gefona nor tafuna as a nexiom (5 cases), or the "both nexioms" rule (3 cases).

TEST: gefona, tafuna
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Eight explanations fit both results so far.

**If the machine needs one nexiom:** neither gefona nor tafuna can be a nexiom, and at least one of suvuben or motufos must be. That leaves 5 pairs:
- suvuben + motufos
- suvuben + neterus
- suvuben + nigogik
- motufos + neterus
- motufos + nigogik

**If the machine needs two nexioms:** both must be among gefona, suvuben and motufos. Any such pair is consistent with gefona + tafuna staying dark. That leaves 3 pairs:
- gefona + suvuben
- gefona + motufos
- suvuben + motufos

Testing suvuben with neterus splits these 8 evenly:
- **Lights up (4 cases):** only possible under the one-nexiom rule, with suvuben or neterus as a nexiom. The pairs are suvuben + motufos, suvuben + neterus, suvuben + nigogik and motufos + neterus.
- **Stays dark (4 cases):** either the one-nexiom rule with motufos + nigogik, or any of the 3 two-nexiom pairs.

TEST: suvuben, neterus
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Four explanations fit all three results so far.

**If the machine needs one nexiom:** suvuben and neterus are ruled out by the last test. Gefona and tafuna were already ruled out. That leaves only motufos + nigogik.

**If the machine needs two nexioms:** the earlier pairs gefona + suvuben, gefona + motufos and suvuben + motufos all still fit. Suvuben + neterus stayed dark because neterus is not a nexiom.

Testing gefona with motufos splits these 4 evenly:
- **Lights up (2 cases):** either the one-nexiom rule with motufos + nigogik, or the two-nexiom rule with gefona + motufos.
- **Stays dark (2 cases):** the two-nexiom rule with either gefona + suvuben or suvuben + motufos.

One more test after that will settle it.

TEST: gefona, motufos
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Two explanations fit all four results so far. Both need two nexioms.

- **Gefona + suvuben:** fits every test. Gefona + motufos stayed dark because suvuben was not on the machine.
- **Suvuben + motufos:** also fits every test.

Testing gefona with suvuben settles it:
- **Lights up:** the nexioms are gefona and suvuben.
- **Stays dark:** the nexioms are suvuben and motufos.

TEST: gefona, suvuben
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine lit up with gefona and suvuben together, so the nexioms are gefona and suvuben.

This machine needs both nexioms on it to light up. Every earlier test that stayed dark had at most one of the two on the machine.

The "one nexiom" rule is ruled out. Under it, the dark tests would have eliminated gefona (with tafuna) and suvuben (with neterus), so this last test could not have lit up.

ANSWER: nexioms = gefona, suvuben; needs = two

messages.content:
New machine. Its objects are: sepobel, sutufin, domipel, lubusi, kafoga, tadaze.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects (three of the six). That splits the 30 possibilities (15 possible pairs × 2 rules) into two equal halves of 15.

TEST: sepobel, sutufin, domipel
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

Since the first test did not light up, 15 possibilities remain:
- **If the machine needs one nexiom:** neither nexiom is among sepobel, sutufin or domipel. Both must be among lubusi, kafoga and tadaze, which gives 3 possible pairs.
- **If it needs two:** the pair just can't be entirely inside {sepobel, sutufin, domipel}, which leaves 12 possible pairs.

My next test is {sepobel, sutufin, lubusi, kafoga}:
- **Needs one:** every remaining pair includes lubusi or kafoga, so it would always light. That is 3 cases.
- **Needs two:** it lights only if both nexioms are in this set. That covers 5 of the 12 pairs.

So "lit" leaves 8 cases and "not lit" leaves 7, which is close to an even split.

TEST: sepobel, sutufin, lubusi, kafoga
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Eight possibilities remain:
- **If the machine needs one nexiom:** the pair is lubusi + kafoga, lubusi + tadaze, or kafoga + tadaze.
- **If it needs two:** the pair is sepobel + lubusi, sepobel + kafoga, sutufin + lubusi, sutufin + kafoga, or lubusi + kafoga. Both nexioms had to be in test 2 but not both in test 1.

My next test is {sepobel, lubusi, tadaze}:
- **It lights** in all three "needs one" cases, and in the "needs two" case sepobel + lubusi. That is 4 cases.
- **It stays dark** for the "needs two" pairs sepobel + kafoga, sutufin + lubusi, sutufin + kafoga and lubusi + kafoga. That is also 4 cases.

So this splits the remaining possibilities evenly.

TEST: sepobel, lubusi, tadaze
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Test 3 rules out the "needs one" rule. Under that rule every remaining pair included lubusi or tadaze, so it would have lit. It also rules out sepobel + lubusi.

The machine needs two nexioms, and four pairs remain:
- sepobel + kafoga
- sutufin + lubusi
- sutufin + kafoga
- lubusi + kafoga

My next test is {sepobel, sutufin, kafoga}:
- **It lights** for sepobel + kafoga or sutufin + kafoga.
- **It stays dark** for sutufin + lubusi or lubusi + kafoga.

That splits the four pairs evenly, two and two.

TEST: sepobel, sutufin, kafoga
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Test 4 did not light, so neither sutufin + kafoga nor sepobel + kafoga is the pair. That leaves two possibilities, both under the "needs two" rule:
- sutufin + lubusi
- lubusi + kafoga

Testing {sutufin, lubusi} decides it. It lights only if those two are the nexioms; otherwise the pair is lubusi + kafoga.

TEST: sutufin, lubusi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Test 5 did not light, so sutufin + lubusi is ruled out. The only possibility left is lubusi + kafoga under the "needs two" rule.

This fits every result:
- **Test 1** (sepobel, sutufin, domipel): neither nexiom present, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 2** (sepobel, sutufin, lubusi, kafoga): both nexioms present, so it lit.
- **Test 3** (sepobel, lubusi, tadaze): only lubusi present, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 4** (sepobel, sutufin, kafoga): only kafoga present, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 5** (sutufin, lubusi): only lubusi present, so it stayed dark.

ANSWER: nexioms = lubusi, kafoga; needs = two

messages.content:
New machine. Its objects are: tibegak, tuditur, bigatel, kafoba, tifanur, lazumun.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

With 6 objects there are 15 possible nexiom pairs and 2 possible rules, so 30 possibilities in total. Testing three objects splits these evenly:
- **If the machine needs one nexiom:** it stays dark only when both nexioms are among the other three (3 of the 15 pairs).
- **If it needs two:** it lights only when both nexioms are among these three (3 pairs).

Either way, light or dark each leaves 15 possibilities.

TEST: tibegak, tuditur, bigatel
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

After the first test, 15 possibilities remain:
- **Needs one nexiom:** any pair with at least one nexiom among tibegak, tuditur, bigatel (12 pairs).
- **Needs two:** both nexioms among those three (3 pairs).

Testing tibegak + kafoba:
- **Needs one:** it lights for 7 of the 12 pairs (5 that include tibegak, plus tuditur–kafoba and bigatel–kafoba) and stays dark for 5.
- **Needs two:** it can't light, because tibegak–kafoba isn't one of the 3 remaining pairs. All 3 go dark.

That gives 7 lit versus 8 dark, a near-even split.

TEST: tibegak, kafoba
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

After two tests, 8 possibilities remain. The second test rules out tibegak and kafoba under the needs-one rule.
- **Needs one:** at least one nexiom is tuditur or bigatel, and neither is tibegak or kafoba. That leaves tuditur–bigatel, tuditur–tifanur, tuditur–lazumun, bigatel–tifanur and bigatel–lazumun (5 pairs).
- **Needs two:** tibegak–tuditur, tibegak–bigatel or tuditur–bigatel (3 pairs).

Testing tuditur + tifanur:
- **Lights:** needs one, with the pair being tuditur–bigatel, tuditur–tifanur, tuditur–lazumun or bigatel–tifanur (4 cases).
- **Stays dark:** needs one with bigatel–lazumun, or any of the 3 needs-two pairs (4 cases).

That is an even 4/4 split, leaving 3 tests to settle 4 cases.

TEST: tuditur, tifanur
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Four possibilities remain after three tests. The third test ruled out tuditur and tifanur under the needs-one rule, and tuditur–tifanur isn't a needs-two candidate.
- **Needs one:** bigatel–lazumun.
- **Needs two:** tibegak–tuditur, tibegak–bigatel or tuditur–bigatel.

Testing tibegak + bigatel:
- **Lights:** either needs one with bigatel–lazumun, or needs two with tibegak–bigatel (2 cases).
- **Stays dark:** needs two with tibegak–tuditur or tuditur–bigatel (2 cases).

That is an even 2/2 split, and one more test can then separate the last two cases.

TEST: tibegak, bigatel
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Two possibilities remain, both under the needs-two rule. The fourth test ruled out bigatel–lazumun (needs one) and tibegak–bigatel (needs two).
- **Tibegak–tuditur.**
- **Tuditur–bigatel.**

Testing tibegak + tuditur settles it:
- **Lights:** the nexioms are tibegak and tuditur.
- **Stays dark:** the nexioms are tuditur and bigatel.

TEST: tibegak, tuditur
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine lit with tibegak and tuditur together, so those two are the nexioms. It needs both of them together. This fits every result:
- **Test 1 (tibegak, tuditur, bigatel):** both nexioms were present, so it lit.
- **Test 2 (tibegak, kafoba):** only one nexiom, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 3 (tuditur, tifanur):** only one nexiom, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 4 (tibegak, bigatel):** only one nexiom, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 5 (tibegak, tuditur):** both nexioms, so it lit.

ANSWER: nexioms = tibegak, tuditur; needs = two

messages.content:
New machine. Its objects are: lilekin, gavozir, basugek, fadosos, davanir, pagedu.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects. This splits the 30 possible answers (15 pairs × 2 rules) evenly between "lit" and "not lit".

TEST: lilekin, gavozir, basugek
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine lit up, so 15 possibilities remain:
- **"Needs one" rule:** at least one nexiom is among lilekin, gavozir and basugek. That gives 12 pairs.
- **"Needs two" rule:** both nexioms are among those three. That gives 3 pairs.

Testing lilekin with fadosos splits these about evenly:
- **If it lights (7 cases):** the rule is "needs one", and the pair includes lilekin or fadosos. Under "needs two" it can't light, because no remaining pair is exactly lilekin and fadosos.
- **If it stays dark (8 cases):** either the rule is "needs one" with a pair drawn from gavozir, basugek, davanir and pagedu (5 cases), or the rule is "needs two" (3 cases).

TEST: lilekin, fadosos
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

After two tests, 8 possibilities remain:
- **"Needs one" rule:** the pair avoids lilekin and fadosos and includes gavozir or basugek. That leaves gavozir+basugek, gavozir+davanir, gavozir+pagedu, basugek+davanir or basugek+pagedu (5 cases).
- **"Needs two" rule:** both nexioms are among lilekin, gavozir and basugek. That leaves lilekin+gavozir, lilekin+basugek or gavozir+basugek (3 cases).

Testing gavozir with davanir splits these evenly:
- **If it lights (4 cases):** the rule is "needs one", and the pair is gavozir+basugek, gavozir+davanir, gavozir+pagedu or basugek+davanir. Under "needs two" it can't light, because no remaining pair is exactly gavozir and davanir.
- **If it stays dark (4 cases):** either the rule is "needs one" with basugek+pagedu, or the rule is "needs two" with any of its 3 pairs.

TEST: gavozir, davanir
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

After three tests, the rule must be "needs one", because only that rule fits the results so far. Four pairs remain:
- gavozir + basugek
- gavozir + davanir
- gavozir + pagedu
- basugek + davanir

Testing basugek alone splits these in half:
- **If it lights:** the pair is gavozir+basugek or basugek+davanir.
- **If it stays dark:** the pair is gavozir+davanir or gavozir+pagedu.

In either case, testing davanir next will settle it.

TEST: basugek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Basugek is not a nexiom, so two pairs remain:
- gavozir + davanir
- gavozir + pagedu

Testing davanir alone settles it:
- **If it lights:** the pair is gavozir + davanir.
- **If it stays dark:** the pair is gavozir + pagedu.

TEST: davanir
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Davanir did not light up on its own, so it is not a nexiom. That leaves only one possibility: **gavozir and pagedu**, with the machine needing just one nexiom.

This fits every result:
- **Test 1 (lilekin, gavozir, basugek):** gavozir is on the machine, so it lit.
- **Test 2 (lilekin, fadosos):** neither is a nexiom, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 3 (gavozir, davanir):** gavozir lit it alone, which only works under the "needs one" rule.
- **Tests 4 and 5 (basugek, then davanir):** neither is a nexiom, so both stayed dark.

ANSWER: nexioms = gavozir, pagedu; needs = one
